subject: Response budget and measurement-window clarification for Hosted API commitments
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara@brightwave.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightwave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify p50/p95 windows and "response budget" in the SLOs

Rishi — thanks again for the call yesterday. Procurement and engineering at Brightwave want to confirm two items before we move to final approval: 

1) Measurement window for p95 — are you measuring p95 over a rolling 1-hour window or a 24-hour epoch? Our legal team flagged the contract language that says "p95 measured over typical production epoch" and we'd like a firm definition.

2) The term you used, "response budget", sounded like a per-request token cap / expected CPU budget. Can you explain how that maps to the p50/p95 targets in practice (e.g., do larger inputs get excluded, or do you normalize)?

We want to avoid surprise SLA credits later. If you can send a short write-up and any sample calc we can show our infra team, that would be great.

Thanks —
Sara
Sara Li
Director, Platform Engineering
Brightwave Inc

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara@brightwave.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Brightwave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 windows and "response budget" in the SLOs

Sara — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, details & a sample workbook attached. [attachment: response_budget_calc.xlsx]

- Measurement window: p50 is calculated on a rolling 5-minute window for alerting/operational thresholds; contractual p95 is measured daily using a 24-hour rolling epoch aligned to UTC (we report a calendar-day p95 aggregated from all requests in that day). We'll add explicit wording to the contract: "p95 is calculated per UTC calendar day; p50 is measured as a rolling 5-minute operational percentile for monitoring."

- Response budget: this is an internal construct we use to translate model/sequence-length variability into expected service time. In practice we:
  * bucket requests by token-length (0-128, 129-512, 513-2048, >2048)
  * apply a per-bucket median (p50) and tail (p95) baseline measured on the selected model variant
  * normalize by a compute multiplier for quantized variants or GPU type.

The attached workbook demonstrates a sample Brightwave traffic mix and shows how we compute a daily expected token-weighted p95 and the implied unit cost.

Next steps I propose:
1) Accept the UTC calendar-day p95 language for the contract.
2) We provide a short appendix that lists the bucketing thresholds and the normalization multipliers for the model family you selected.
3) If Brightwave needs a different measurement epoch (e.g., local business-day), we can add a regional addendum and map to a regional fallback.

I'll loop in Lauren for the contractual language.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara@brightwave.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Brightwave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 windows and "response budget" in the SLOs

Sara — adding the contractual wording here so you can paste directly into your draft: 

"Latency SLO definitions: For Hosted API, "p95 latency" refers to the 95th percentile of end-to-end request latency for all successful requests within a UTC calendar day (00:00:00–23:59:59 UTC). Reported p95 is computed from production traffic logs and excludes requests that meet documented carve-outs (maintenance windows, operator-initiated bulk imports, and authenticated test keys identified in the appendix). The Provider maintains operational p50 measurements on a rolling 5-minute window for monitoring and incident response purposes; these monitoring metrics are not used for contractual breach calculations"

Regarding "response budget" — we recommend including the following appendix entry in Section X (Operational Definitions):
  - "Response budget: a token-length-weighted latency baseline used for capacity planning and burst mitigation. Requests are bucketed by input+output token length per the thresholds below. For each bucket the Provider publishes an expected median and 95th percentile baseline for the selected model family. When assessing SLA compliance, requests in the >2048 token bucket may be subject to different routing and are reported separately."

We can attach SLO text as a PDF if useful. Draft attached: [attachment: slo_proposal_v2.pdf]

Happy to iterate on wording — if your legal team prefers a different epoch (e.g., 24-hour rolling vs calendar-day), state the preference and we'll mark it as an exception path with explicit measurement mapping and any credit calculation changes.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success — Hosted Products
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Li <sara@brightwave.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Brightwave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 windows and "response budget" in the SLOs

Thanks Rishi & Lauren — that helps a lot. A couple quick follow-ups from our infra and legal teams: 

- Legal wants the p95 calendar-day language in the SLA; infra prefers a 24-hour rolling epoch for operational signal (they will accept calendar-day for contract). Please include both definitions (as you already have) and an explicit mapping for how credits would be calculated if an event spans a UTC boundary.

- Infra flagged the >2048 token bucket as a potential exception: can you confirm whether requests routed to Dedicated-only variants (or routed to a fallback lower-capacity quantized model) will be excluded from contractual p95? We need clarity because our workflows include occasional multi-document summarization jobs.

If you can add a one-paragraph note on carve-outs for model-variant routing and a sample credit calculation for a cross-boundary event, procurement can proceed to finalize. We expect to sign by end of week once the addendum is added.

I'll attach our internal checklist for SLO language so you can align the appendix.

—Sara
